claim.title: Finite-d bias exactness: E[beta_hat] = gamma*beta at finite d (repairs C2's circular bias check)
claim.statement: For d=150, sigma=0.1, ||beta||_2=1, isotropic Gaussian features, the Monte-Carlo estimate of E[beta_hat] over T=200 trials is parallel to beta within 5% (|<E[beta_hat], beta_perp>|/||beta|| < 0.05) and its coefficient along beta is within 2% relative error of gamma, for every gamma in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9} with n=floor(gamma*d).
claim.test_plan: Self-contained numpy script: d=150, beta=e_1, sigma=0.1, gamma in {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9}, T=200 trials each; per trial X~N(0,I), y=X@beta+sigma*noise, beta_hat=X.T@solve(XX.T,y); accumulate sum_beta_hat. E_hat=sum/T. coefs = <E_hat, beta> (should equal gamma); ortho = sqrt(||E_hat||^2 - coefs^2) (should be ~0). Control: at gamma=0.5 the coefficient must be 0.5 within 2% (a case where the projection-averaging argument is simplest); if the control fails the measurement is void.
claim.success_criterion: For all 5 gamma values: |coef - gamma|/gamma <= 0.02 and ortho <= 0.05; control at gamma=0.5 passes.
claim.rationale: In C2 round 2 the bias metric (max_rel_err_B=3.4e-15) was computed from a hard-coded E[beta_hat]=gamma*beta, i.e. the bias formula was compared against itself. This variant re-derives E[beta_hat] from raw Monte-Carlo means, so the claim's bias formula B_n=(1-gamma)^2||beta||^2 is verified independently (it is in fact exact at any finite d under isotropy; the 'approximation' is in variance/risk only).
claim.evidence_in_paper: agent-generated variant of C2 (repairs its circular bias check)
